title: 26 Evaluating the effect of Livamol with BioWorma in controlling gastrointestinal nematodes and improving performance in does during late pregnancy and early lactation
content:
Abstract
Gastrointestinal nematodes (GIN) affect goats’ health, production rates, and profit. Anthelmintic resistance developed in GIN has led to the need for an alternative method to control them. BioWorma is considered to reduce GIN prevalence in small ruminants. However, its effect has not been evaluated in animals around parturition when their immunity becomes critical. This study tested the hypothesis that using Livamol with BioWorma would decrease GIN loads and improve performance in does around parturition. The objective of the study was to evaluate the effect of Livamol with BioWorma on GIN loads and performance in does around parturition. Kiko does (n=14) in their late pregnancy (3rd trimester) were split into Control and BioWorma groups. The Control group received 0.23kg. of whole corn and the BioWorma group received 0.23kg. of whole corn and Livamol with BioWorma (0.05kg/45.36kg. live weight). Both groups had one water trough, 2 mobile shelters, one mineral feeder, and one supplement feeder. Each group was rotationally grazed in separate sets of plots (4 plots/group) from March to July 2024. Animal performance (live weight, body condition score, and FAMACHA score) and fecal samples were collected on the first day, weekly, and the last day of the study. Fecal samples were analyzed using McMaster’s Methods. McMaster’s Methods were conducted by weighing 0.002kg of fecal sample. Next, a salt solution was added so the total weight was 0.03kg, the solid particles were broken using a tongue depressor, and the solution was mixed until uniform. The solution was strained, placed in a test tube, and rested for 6 minutes. A pipette was used to obtain the solution and placed into both chambers of the McMaster’s slide. Data were analyzed in SAS 9.4. GIN EPG of animal feces was analyzed using the NPAR1WAY Procedure and animal performance was analyzed using the GLM procedure. Live weight and BCS were similar for both groups. FAMACHA scores were similar except for two observation dates. On March 28th (week 2), the BioWorma group had a higher FAMACHA score (3.2%, P< 0.01). On April 26th (week 6), the Control group had a higher FAMACHA score (8.3%, P< 0.05). Fecal EPG values remained similar in both groups, except for a few observation dates. On April 26th (week 6), June 28th (week 15), and July 5th (week 16) the Control group had higher mean EPG values (49.6%, P< 0.05; 55.2%, P< 0.05; and 61.1%, P< 0.05, respectively). On May 3rd (week 7) and June 7th (week 12) the BioWorma group had higher mean EPG values (89.6%, P< 0.01 and 59.6%, P< 0.05, respectively). Results showed that the use of Livamol with BioWorma may not be a good option for controlling GIN and improving performance in Kiko does during the peripartum period.
